choices.misconception: I counted 10 down instead of 10 up.
I added 1 to 38 instead of adding 10.
I added 1 to both digits of 38.
I thought 10 more means writing a 0 on the end of the number.

hints: Which digit changes when you add 10?
Adding 10 adds one more ten. Only the tens digit goes up, and the ones digit stays the same.
38 has 3 tens and 8 ones. One more ten makes 4 tens and still 8 ones.

solutions.reliable: 38 is 3 tens and 8 ones. Adding 10 gives 4 tens and 8 ones, which is 48. The idea to keep: adding 10 raises the tens digit by one and leaves the ones digit alone.
solutions.elegant: On a hundred square, 10 more is the square straight below, and below 38 is 48.

whyOnTest: Adding 10 tests place value directly, and changing the ones digit instead is the common mistake.
